calls.title: GrowthBook - PhonePe
calls.summary: The team addressed significant data synchronization discrepancies in Growth Book, where user query counts showed a mismatch between 107 million and 14,000 in the UI, indicating a core issue. Luke Sonnet proposed that data arriving out of timestamp order might be the cause, leading to a discussion on verifying sequential data loading in Hive. Additionally, the inefficiency of the full load query, which currently takes 17 hours due to scanning legacy tables, was highlighted, prompting suggestions for consolidating metrics into a single fact table. The team also discussed the organization-level control of incremental updates and the need for dimension handling due to excess distinct values. Koushik Roy committed to sharing necessary queries and schema details for further review, prioritizing the resolution of the user count mismatch before broader data model enhancements.
calls.keywords: Growth Book, incremental load, Hive data modeling, user deduplication, experiment validation, query optimization

calls.title: GrowthBook - PhonePe
calls.summary: The discussion revolved around addressing key blockers in scaling GrowthBook, specifically regarding the monitoring of ETL completion and the sequencing of data refresh. Koushik highlighted the need for a unified screen displaying ETL status across multiple experiments, while Luke suggested using API-triggered updates after ETL completes to ensure data readiness. Maintaining simultaneous experiment start times through API control was emphasized to preserve existing workflows. Additionally, issues like variability in query counts due to initial loads and the lack of built-in alerting for failed updates were acknowledged, with plans for improvements in these areas. Archiving inactive experiments to improve performance and establishing an upgrade process via Docker deployment were also outlined as critical steps moving forward.
